title_prefix: Header-index delta replay leaves two obj
mechanism: %replay-header-index-delta parses each delta record into a BRAND-NEW block-index-entry and installs it with (setf (gethash hash index) e) (src/storage/chain.lisp:1234-1239), then relinks with (link-header-entries index prev-all) where prev-all holds ONLY the prev hashes the delta itself carried (chain.lisp:1240-1242). link-header-entries iterates prev-hash-map, so it touches nothing outside the delta (chain.lisp:1405-1412). Any entry that was in the snapshot and did NOT change therefore keeps its prev-entry pointing at the SUPERSEDED object for a parent the delta refreshed, and the two objects then differ on every mutable field: status, tx-count, file, data-pos, undo-pos. The load is by hash but every ancestry walk follows prev-entry -- get-block-at-height walks back from the tip (chain.lisp:423-433), entry-ancestor-at-height (chain.lisp:136-144), collect-chain-entries (src/validation/block.lisp:2889-2899), build-block-locator (chain.lisp:1416-1436) -- and %changed-header-index-entries / %write-header-index-snapshot only ever maphash the table (chain.lisp:1039-1045,1058-1067), so a write through a walk is invisible to BOTH the live entry and the persisted index. The reachable producer of the shape (a parent refreshed while its child is not) is pruning: forget-undo-data clears file/data-pos/undo-pos on an OLD entry whose already-connected child has not changed since the last full snapshot (src/validation/block.lisp:2150-2167), which is Core's PruneOneBlockFile behaviour; the lazy tx-count backfill on old entries (src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:1568-1582) and invalidateblock/reconsiderblock on an old block do the same. Core cannot reach it: LoadBlockIndexGuts materialises every CBlockIndex through BlockManager::InsertBlockIndex, a try_emplace on m_block_index, and resolves each pprev through the SAME function, so there is exactly one object per hash (refs/bitcoin/src/node/blockstorage.cpp:407-421,425-426). Note the precondition the finding does not state: a clean shutdown force-fulls the snapshot and DELETES the delta (src/node/shutdown.lisp:368, chain.lisp:1046-1048), so replay -- and therefore the split -- requires an unclean stop with a non-empty delta.
consequence: For the whole life of a process started on a replayed delta, the block index holds two contradictory copies of every entry the delta refreshed whose child it did not, and the prev-entry graph -- not the hash table -- is what every ancestry walk returns. Executed: (a) two-entry case, index[A] came back :INVALID / data-pos 4242 while B's prev-entry came back :VALID / data-pos 100 and was not EQ to index[A]; (b) active-chain case, a 4-block chain with the height-2 body pruned, collect-chain-entries from the tip returned an entry that was NOT EQ to the live one and still reported data-pos 200 while the live entry reported NIL, and applying %reorg-disconnect's own (setf status :header-valid) over the walked list left the live entry :VALID with %changed-header-index-entries seeing 2 changed entries instead of 3. Three consequences follow from that one split. Status writes taken from a reorg walk (%reorg-disconnect src/validation/block.lisp:3424, %reorg-connect :3532) are dropped from headerindex.dat, so the persisted index can record :valid for a block that was disconnected. Readers that take a flat-file position off a walked entry (the index catch-up loops in src/storage/txindex.lisp:341, blockfilterindex.lisp:265, coinstatsindex.lisp:340 and the getblock/REST height paths) get a stale data-pos for a body that pruning deleted. And dumptxoutset's rollback guard compares identity, not hash -- (unless (eq (bl.store:get-block-at-height chain-state target-height) target-entry) ... "Block is not in the active chain") at src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:996-999 -- so a hash-resolved rollback target that IS on the active chain is refused, an operator-visible wrong refusal. Bounded below S1 because the hashes, heights and headers on the orphan are correct (so PoW, MTP, locator and descends-from answers are unaffected) and the next full snapshot plus restart rebuilds a consistent graph.
evidence: Probes under build/ga11v/p2-orphan.lisp, loaded into BITCOIN-LISP.TESTS and run with scripts/dev.sh eval on the project container in worktree bl-ga11v-storage-s2, reproducing the finder's two cases independently. (1) ga11v-p2a: snapshot A(:valid, data-pos 100) and child B, then A -> :invalid + data-pos 4242, delta, reload -> (:INDEX-A-STATUS :INVALID :INDEX-A-DATA-POS 4242 :B-PREV-STATUS :VALID :B-PREV-DATA-POS 100 :B-PREV-EQ-INDEX-A NIL). (2) ga11v-p2b: four linked :valid entries with positions, snapshot, height-2 entry pruned (file/data-pos/undo-pos cleared, exactly forget-undo-data's writes), delta, reload -> (:WALK-HEIGHTS (4 3 2) :WALKED-A-EQ-LIVE-A NIL :WALKED-A-DATA-POS 200 :LIVE-A-DATA-POS NIL :LIVE-A-STATUS-AFTER-WALK-WRITE :VALID :WALKED-A-STATUS-AFTER-WALK-WRITE :HEADER-VALID :CHANGED-ENTRIES-SEEN-BY-SAVE 2 :WALK-LENGTH 3). Ours: src/storage/chain.lisp:136-144,423-433,1039-1067,1163-1250,1405-1412,1416-1436,1447-1452; src/validation/block.lisp:2150-2167,2889-2899,3424,3532; src/rpc/blockchain.lisp:996-999,1568-1582; src/storage/txindex.lisp:341; src/node/shutdown.lisp:368. Core at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/node/blockstorage.cpp:407-421,425-426.
fix_shape: Do not implement here. Port InsertBlockIndex's invariant rather than patching the relink: replay must MUTATE the existing entry for a hash instead of installing a second object. In %replay-header-index-delta, after reading a record, look the hash up in the index and, when it is already there, copy the record's mutable fields (status, tx-count, file, data-pos, undo-pos, and the header if the format carries it) into the existing entry, leaving its identity and its children's prev-entry pointers alone; only a hash that is genuinely new gets a fresh entry, and only those need the prev-all relink pass. That also removes the need for read-single-header-entry to build a second table at all for known hashes. Pin it with a structural test that the object graph is single-valued after a replay -- for every entry, (eq (block-index-entry-prev-entry child) (get-block-index-entry state parent-hash)) -- run over a fixture whose delta refreshes a parent whose child it does not, with the positive control that the assertion fails on the pre-fix replay. Separately worth its own line: dumptxoutset's rollback guard should compare block hashes like entry-on-active-chain-p and %block-on-active-chain-p do, not object identity, since a hash-resolved entry and a walked entry are only ever EQ by construction.
